newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal banks seek intervention for NOC oil payment.
newsitem.headline: Nepal banks seek intervention for NOC oil payment.

text.p: Nepalese banks are seeking the intervention of the country's central bank to meet dollar demand by the state-owned oil firm to pay an import bill, dealers said on Thursday.
Banks did not quote any rates for the Nepali rupee against dollar on Thursday, expecting the central bank to intervene and decide rates, they said. On Wednesday, the dollar closed at 56.90/92 rupees.

Bankers said the supply of dollars in the interbank market has dried up and banks have requested the central bank to intervene to meet the demand by the state-owned Nepal Oil Corporation (NOC). "NOC needs $8 million to pay for the import of petroleum products," one banker said.
Nepal Rastra Bank, the kingdom's central bank, quoted its rupee-dollar rate at 56.75-57.30 rupees per dollar.
Inter-bank call money rates opened at 9.00-9.30 percent on Thursday, compared to the previous close of 9.35 percent, dealers said.
